criteria.criterion: A duplicate-title metric counts same-normalized-title creations over a window, derived from the SAME pure recent_creates.normalize_title() predicate duplicate_warning uses.
A creation-VOLUME metric counts ticket CREATE events per hour, independent of title. Without this the alarm misses the incident that prompted it.
Both are published by an observer that does NOT depend on the bridge running, demonstrated with reconciliation stopped.

Alarms fire on rates consistent with mass creation, not ordinary operation. Justify against the RCA numbers: duplicate baseline 0-2/day vs 88/hr, so count > 10 per rolling hour; volume baseline 4-9/hr vs 968 fixed UTC-hour bucket / 1010 rolling-hour replay.

`treat_missing_data`, `evaluation_periods` and `datapoints_to_alarm` chosen against measured cadence, with reasoning recorded, and an explicit statement of why the combination cannot reproduce `illbred-sour-alpaca`'s false-page or unclearable-alarm behaviour.
No clamping anywhere in either metric path.
Defect-seeded: synthesise a burst in a test store, confirm each metric rises and its alarm condition is met; remove it and confirm it clears.
Replay proof against the CORRECT window: 2026-08-31 06:00Z - 2026-09-01 04:00Z (replay oracle: duplicate peak_hour=85; volume window 2026-09-04 21:25Z onward with peak_hour=1010).
Portability: local store read plus host metric publish; no dependence on any single CI provider.
Bug 'Duplicate ticket creation is detectable in rebar but nothing aggregates or alarms on it' is actually resolved: the reported defect no longer reproduces.

citations.description: Contains only synthetic seeded tests; no historical replay assertions against the 2026-08-31 or 2026-09-04 windows.

findings.criterion: Replay proof against the CORRECT window: 2026-08-31 06:00Z - 2026-09-01 04:00Z (replay oracle: duplicate peak_hour=85 after false-positive suppressions; day buckets 233+172=405; 425 is store-wide all-time excess) for the duplicate detector, and the 2026-09-04 21:25Z onward surge for the volume detector. If either would not have fired, the threshold or the signal is wrong — say so rather than adjusting the criterion.
findings.detail: No historical replay tests exist in the repository. Searched tests/ for '2026-08-31', 'peak_hour == 85', 'peak_hour == 1010', and 'replay' — none found in test files. The test_event_metrics.py file contains only synthetic/seeded unit tests (burst of 12 same-title tickets, burst of 51 distinct-title tickets) but no tests that replay the actual historical store windows and assert the oracle values (duplicate peak_hour=85, volume peak_hour=1010). The ticket's last comment attests 'historical replay fired duplicate detector for 2026-08-31/09-01 and volume detector for 2026-09-04/05' but this is a non-codebase attestation for a codebase-verifiable criterion (no [non-codebase] tag).
findings.remediation: Add replay tests that load the actual historical store data (or a fixture derived from it) for the windows 2026-08-31T06:00:00Z..2026-09-01T04:00:00Z and 2026-09-04T21:25:00Z..2026-09-05T03:00:00Z, and assert duplicate_title_peak_hour.peak_hour == 85 (alarm=True) and create_volume_peak_hour.peak_hour == 1010 (alarm=True) respectively, plus baseline 2026-08-20..2026-08-25 stays below both thresholds.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[non-codebase]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify. Note that a finding reporting a ticket record as absent means it was NOT VISIBLE IN THE TICKET SNAPSHOT THE VERIFIER READ — that snapshot is pinned when the run starts, so a record written after the pin, or not yet committed to the store, reads as missing even though it exists; re-verify after the write lands rather than re-recording evidence you already wrote.
